binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, equipped with the assumption that mu is a probability measure.
Two arbitrary functions X, Y : Omega → Real.
hypotheses: X is measurable and there exists a real K_X > 0 such that omega ↦ exp(X(omega)^2 / K_X^2) is mu-integrable and has mu-integral at most 2.
Y is measurable and there exists a real K_Y > 0 such that omega ↦ exp(Y(omega)^2 / K_Y^2) is mu-integrable and has mu-integral at most 2.
The ENNReal infimum of all t such that X is measurable, t is neither 0 nor infinity, omega ↦ exp(X(omega)^2 / (t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2, is equal to 1.
The analogous ENNReal infimum of admissible scales for Y is equal to 1.
conclusions: The mu-integral of omega ↦ exp(X(omega)^2) is at most 2.
The mu-integral of omega ↦ exp(Y(omega)^2) is at most 2.
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued measurable function Z and t in ENNReal, call t admissible when t ≠ 0, t ≠ infinity, exp(Z^2/(t.toReal)^2) is mu-integrable, and its mu-integral is at most 2.
Define the scale rho_mu(Z) as inf {t in ENNReal | t is admissible for Z}.
The auxiliary domain hypothesis on Z requires existence of a positive real K for which exp(Z^2/K^2) is mu-integrable and has integral at most 2.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, let X and Y be real-valued functions that are measurable and each admit at least one positive real scale at which its exponential squared moment is integrable and at most 2. For each function, form the extended-nonnegative-real infimum of all nonzero finite scales t at which the same bound holds for exp(Z^2/(t.toReal)^2). If this infimum is exactly 1 for X and exactly 1 for Y, then both unscaled exponential-square integrals satisfy ∫ exp(X^2) dmu ≤ 2 and ∫ exp(Y^2) dmu ≤ 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is required to be a probability measure, and X and Y must satisfy the strong domain hypotheses encoded by LocalDef001; the proposition does not cover arbitrary real-valued functions.
Admissible infimum scales live in ENNReal but are explicitly restricted to be nonzero and finite before conversion to Real; the auxiliary existence witness in LocalDef001 instead has type Real.

Equality of an infimum to 1 does not, merely by the definition of infimum, assert that the scale 1 itself belongs to the admissible set or that the infimum is attained. The conclusion supplies a bound at scale 1 without an explicit attainment hypothesis.

The conclusion states only inequalities involving MeasureTheory.integral and does not explicitly assert Integrable (exp(X^2)) or Integrable (exp(Y^2)); scaled integrability is explicit only inside the antecedent predicates.

Because the integral operator is total, its behavior on nonintegrable functions may make a bare integral inequality weaker or vacuous unless integrability at scale 1 follows from other hypotheses; that behavior is not exposed by the one-level body supplied for MeasureTheory.integral.

X and Y are unrelated: no independence, identical-distribution, equality, sum, product, or other joint relationship is assumed or concluded. The theorem is a conjunction of two separate instances of the same unary statement.
No centering, zero-mean, symmetry, variance normalization, or tail-probability assertion is encoded.
ambiguities: The packet exposes MeasureTheory.integral only through an opaque wrapper body, so its exact totalization behavior on a nonintegrable unscaled exponential is not derivable from the packet alone.

The dossier defines the auxiliary existence condition using positive real scales and the infimum using finite nonzero ENNReal scales, but does not expose any theorem connecting those two formulations; the proposition simply assumes both relevant facts.
The normalization rho_mu(Z) = 1 alone does not reveal whether admissibility at the boundary is intended to be attained; the formal conclusion asserts the boundary inequality regardless.
